task_instance: Given a sample set of Q3 2026 metrics for a fictional Series A SaaS company (Northwind Analytics), build a full quarterly board deck in Markdown following the skill's 11-section structure (Executive Summary, Key Metrics Dashboard, Financial Update, Revenue & Pipeline, Product Update, Growth & Marketing, Engineering & Technical, Team & People, Risk & Security, Strategic Outlook, Appendix), applying the 4-Act narrative framework and the bad-news-delivery framework to the Q3 ARR miss, and using explicit [PLACEHOLDER] markers (never invented numbers) for metrics the sample input did not supply.
evidence: Created input_metrics.md (sample company metrics with explicit list of data gaps) and board_deck_Q3_2026.md (the actual deliverable) in the work directory. The deck file contains all 11 sections from SKILL.md in the specified order, a filled Key Metrics Dashboard table with target/status columns, a written Executive Summary matching the 3-sentence format and 'Good' example style from SKILL.md, the ARR-miss variance explained per the Section-3/bad-news framework (state plainly -> own cause -> show understanding -> present fix -> updated forecast), a completed 4-Act narrative check, and a self-audit against the 'Common Board Deck Mistakes' table. Fields not covered by the sample input (e.g., full P&L breakdown, ARR waterfall components, channel-level CAC, engineering velocity trend, attrition rate) are marked with explicit [PLACEHOLDER] text rather than fabricated, per the skill's own rule ('fills gaps with explicit placeholders -- never invents numbers') and per this run's rule against fabricating missing data. Verified by reading the produced file back and confirming structure, tables, and placeholder markers rendered correctly. Note: the skill's two referenced supporting files (references/deck-frameworks.md, templates/board-deck-template.md) were not present alongside SKILL.md, but they were not needed to achieve the core deliverable since SKILL.md itself contains the full deck structure, narrative framework, and bad-news framework inline; the fundraising-specific Sequoia format (which does live only in the missing reference file) was not needed because the chosen task instance was a standard quarterly deck, not a fundraising deck. The entire task required only reading/writing text files -- no code execution, binaries, or network/connector access were needed.
